title: Pinecone-Derived Activated Carbons as an Effective Medium for Hydrogen Storage
material_description: DPC | dehydrated pinecone powder: Pinus pinea cones washed with distilled water, dried 12 h at 353 K, milled, then heated at 453 K for 5 h in air; KOH/DPC = 0 (not KOH-activated)
source_location: main p.4, Table 1, DPC row, column i (H2 wt%, 77 K and 1 bar)
notes: Printed 0.00. No plotted isotherm for DPC. H2 0–1 bar measured with the Micromeritics ASAP 2460 (volumetric); free-volume determination not described. Figure 8 shows the DPC point at 0 wt% with an error bar (not printed numerically). Conflicts with the text 'as low as 0.38 wt% in the DPC sample' (separate row). Not grouped with the DPC 80-bar value: the paper measured 0–1 bar and 0–80 bar on different instruments. | BET range: 0.05–0.15 (relative pressure; Table 1 footnote a and Section 2.2). N2 77 K (Micromeritics ASAP 2460); VT single-point at P/P0 = 0.99 per Table 1 footnote b (Section 2.2 says 0.995); Vmicro, ultra-micropore (<7 Å, stored with 0.7 nm cutoff) and super-micropore volumes from DFT (slit-shaped pores) cumulative volume; Vmeso = pores below 500 Å. Degassing before H2 measurements printed as '≈473 K overnight' (stored 199.85 °C = 473 − 273.15; duration not numeric); N2 samples were treated at 473 K for 12 h in vacuum. wt% defined in Section 2.2 as 'weight percent of adsorbed gas per gram of adsorbent' (coded W1, stated). The paper says DPC showed no appreciable N2 uptake. Text claim that all PSDs peak near 0.5 nm is not applied to DPC (Figure S2 DPC peak lies near 15 Å).
